court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Rukmini W/O. Sitaram Kale And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Rukmini W/O. Sitaram Kale And Others (wife, applicants)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra and Jayashri (husband's wife, respondent no.2)

facts_of_case: Parties arrived at amicable settlement; FIR bearing crime No.173 of 2017 registered with Sengaon Police Station, District Hingoli for the offence punishable under sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash a criminal proceeding or complaint or FIR may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute.
legal_principles.held: However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.
cited_cases: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

legal_principles.principle: Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.
cited_cases: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

outcome.final_order: FIR quashed; parties have arrived at amicable settlement and thus filed a joint settlement purshis in HMP No.A-340 of 2020 before the Family Court, Aurangabad.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
